title: Arithmetic Unitarity III: in Search of Positivity — G5, Polarization, and Hilbert Versus Krein
summary: Volume I (ai.viXra:2610.0045v2) showed that the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is equivalent to unitarity (the absence of negative-norm ("ghost") directions) of the logarithmic scaling flow for the Weil form Q; Volume II measured that obstruction on the Weil form itself. This volume asks which structure could supply the positivity. For curves over F_q, Weil's proof needs a commutative algebra containing Frobenius, an involution with F F^dagger = q, a trace for which the involution is positive, and Albert's algebraic step. review.reason: Examines which structures could give positivity for the Weil form, comparing Hilbert and Krein spaces.
